clauses.why: Only arises because the spec makes the schedule owner-editable; a fixed schedule never meets this question.
An owner-editable schedule is not asked for; a builder could ship a fixed schedule and the reminders would work.
Validation limits exist only because the spec introduced an owner-editable schedule.
Offset validation exists only because the spec introduced an owner-editable schedule.
Ordering validation exists only because the spec introduced an owner-editable schedule.
Owner-configurable send time and time zone are not called for; fixed values would deliver the requested reminders.
Error messages for settings changes only matter because the spec added owner-editable settings.
Rejected-change handling only arises from the spec's added owner-editable settings.
Per-invoice opt-out for disputes is a further capability; automatic reminders for unpaid invoices work without it.
Removing a per-invoice mark only exists because the spec added the extra opt-out mark.
A per-invoice reminder history view is an added audit feature; reminders are delivered fine without it.
Running two concurrent copies is a deployment scenario the request never raises; coordinating them costs real work.
Rollback compatibility with a prior version is an operational duty the request's purpose does not call for.
Reinstall-after-revert behaviour is an operational duty beyond the request's purpose.
